topic: Massage for surfers' shoulders and upper back

slides.headline: Paddle muscles need recovery too
slides.sub: Where remedial massage fits for surfers' shoulders and upper back.

slides.title: Where surfers get tight
slides.body: Long paddles load the lats, upper traps, rotator cuff and the muscles between the shoulder blades. Many surfers notice stiffness through the upper back and neck after a big week.

slides.title: What massage can offer
slides.body: Remedial massage can help tight areas feel easier and make moving your shoulders and neck more comfortable. Many people find it a useful way to recover between busy surf days.

slides.title: Time it around surf days
slides.body: A lighter session the day before a big surf, or a more thorough one on a rest day, suits most people. Mention the forecast and your plans when you book.

slides.title: Pair it with strength
slides.body: Massage complements, rather than replaces, shoulder strength work. Rows, band rotations and mid-back mobility on land, a couple of times a week, help your shoulders keep up with all that paddling.

slides.title: Know when it's more than tight
slides.body: Pain with weakness lifting your arm, painful clicking, or pins and needles down the arm may need a physio or GP assessment first. Your therapist will point you in that direction if needed.

slides.headline: Upper back feeling the swell?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists work on the areas surfing loads most and share simple mobility ideas for home. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Big week in the water and your upper back is letting you know about it?

Paddling loads the lats, upper traps, rotator cuff and the muscles between your shoulder blades. After a run of good swells, stiffness through the upper back and neck is really common.

Remedial massage can help those areas feel easier and make moving more comfortable, especially on a rest day. It works well alongside land-based strength work like rows and band rotations, which help your shoulders keep up with the paddling. Pain with weakness or pins and needles down the arm is worth a physio or GP assessment first.

Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy know what surfing asks of your shoulders. Book online via the link in bio.
